title: motion_negative_result
universal_lens: The mapping from pre-snap motion to defensive coverage is not a global bijection but a conditional kernel. The boolean motion flag acts as an observation trigger, while the true predictive signal emerges from the tensor product of down-state, distance, and receiver leverage.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, we model $P(\text{Man} \mid \text{Motion})$ as highly collinear with game state. A conformal inference layer must condition on down/distance; otherwise, the low prevalence (1.7%) and high p-value (0.09) induce severe calibration errors in coverage priors.
gse_mapping: GSE treats motion as a state-transition catalyst rather than a static feature. The engine evaluates defender displacement vectors only when the situational context (3rd/4th down) elevates the expected value of maintaining tight leverage, dynamically updating the man-coverage probability.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by establishing the failure of the global motion operator. We define the event space of plays $\Omega$, with a boolean indicator $M \in \{0,1\}$ for pre-snap motion and a latent coverage variable $C \in \{\text{man}, \text{zone}\}$. The initial hypothesis posits that $M$ is a sufficient statistic for inferring $C$. However, evaluating the joint distribution over 98,579 plays reveals $P(C=\text{man} | M=1) = 0.267$ versus $P(C=\text{man} | M=0) = 0.285$. The chi-square test yields $p=0.091$, failing to reject the null hypothesis of independence. Thus, the marginal utility of $M$ is effectively zero.

To resolve this duality, we introduce the game state vector $S = (d, y)$, representing down and yards to go. Conditioning on $S$ within the subset $M=1$ reveals a stark, monotonic gradient in man-coverage probability: $0.158 \rightarrow 0.258 \rightarrow 0.425 \rightarrow 0.649$ across downs 1 through 4. This demonstrates that $M$ and $C$ are conditionally dependent given $S$. The apparent inertness of motion is an artifact of averaging over a highly heterogeneous state space. The true physical primitive is not the boolean existence of motion, but the kinematic response of the defense—specifically, per-defender displacement vectors. The transition from a team-level flag to a continuous displacement kernel aligns the mathematical model with the underlying biomechanical reality of leverage maintenance on critical downs.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the defensive coordinator as a rational agent optimizing coverage against offensive tendencies. On early downs, the cost of playing man coverage outweighs the benefit of neutralizing motion. However, on 3rd/4th down, the penalty for a successful pass increases exponentially. The coordinator's decision to deploy man coverage becomes highly sensitive to any offensive attempt to disrupt alignment via motion, revealing their intent to maintain strict leverage.
